items.answer: (d) Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true. When current flows through a solenoid, the currents in the various turns of the solenoid are parallel and in the same direction. Since currents flowing through parallel wires in the same direction lead to a force of attraction between them, the turns of the solenoid also attract each other and as a result the solenoid tends to contract.

items.answer: (b) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A). The torque acting on the coil depends on the angle θ between the plane of the coil and the direction of the magnetic field. When θ = 90° then τ = 0, and the coil tries to orient itself in this position. Thus in equilibrium the coil acquires a position such that its plane makes an angle of 90° with the direction of the magnetic field.

items.stem: State the observation made by Oersted on the basis of his experiment with current carrying conductors.
items.answer: Every current carrying conductor has a magnetic field around it.

items.stem: Name the scientist who discovered the earth's magnetic field.
items.answer: William Gilbert.

items.stem: How is the strength of the magnetic field at a point near a wire related to the strength of the electric current flowing in the wire?

items.stem: Does a stationary charge produce a magnetic field?

items.stem: When magnetic lines of force are widely separated, what does it indicate?

items.stem: Why do two magnetic field lines not intersect each other? (or) Explain why two magnetic field lines do not intersect each other. (or) No two magnetic field lines can intersect each other. Explain.
items.answer: If two field lines intersected each other, then at the point of intersection two tangents, and hence two directions of the magnetic field, could be drawn. This is not possible, as the magnetic field can have only one direction at a given point.

items.stem: What is the function of an earth wire? Why is it necessary to earth metallic appliances?
items.answer: The earth wire is connected to a metallic plate deep inside the earth. Thus the metallic body of the appliance is connected to the earth, which provides a low-resistance conducting path for electric current. The user then does not get a severe electric shock on touching such an appliance.

items.stem: Why does an electric short circuit occur?
items.answer: If the plastic insulation of the live wire and the neutral wire gets torn, the two wires touch each other. This direct touching of the live wire and the neutral wire is known as a short circuit. When the two wires touch, the resistance of the circuit so formed is very small, so the current flowing through the wires becomes very large and heats the wires to a high temperature, and a fire may be started.

items.stem: (i) A compass needle gets deflected when brought near a current carrying conductor. Why? (ii) What happens to the deflection of the needle when current in the conductor is increased?
items.answer: (i) A current carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it, which deflects the compass needle. (ii) The deflection increases with an increase in current.

items.stem: Define a solenoid. How is it different from a coil?
items.answer: (i) A coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder is called a solenoid. (ii) The strength of the magnetic field inside a coil varies, while in the case of a solenoid it is the same (uniform).

items.stem: An alternating electric circuit has a frequency of 50 Hz. How many times does it change its direction in one second? Give reason for your answer.
items.answer: 100 times. 50 Hz means 50 cycles per second and one cycle involves two changes of direction, so 50 Hz AC means the current changes its direction 100 times in a second.

items.stem: Compare the pattern of the magnetic field around a solenoid with the magnetic field around a bar magnet.
items.answer: The pattern of the magnetic field around a solenoid looks similar to that around a bar magnet. One end of the solenoid behaves as a north pole while the other behaves as a south pole, and a current carrying solenoid, when freely suspended, rests along the north-south direction just like a bar magnet.

items.stem: Write a few uses of magnets.

items.answer: A compass needle consists of a short and thin magnet pivoted at its centre and enclosed in a glass casing. items.stem: How will you locate the current-carrying wire concealed in a wall?
items.answer: The current-carrying wire concealed in a wall can be located with the help of a compass needle. In the absence of any current, the needle of the magnetic compass stays along the north-south direction; if current is flowing, the needle deflects from its stationary position.
